\subsection{Attribution, value function and conclusions}
\label{sec:setting}
A trained model $f$ maps an instance $x$ with $d$ raw attributes to a score. Each raw attribute is one player; a categorical attribute is one player and is one-hot encoded inside the model wrapper.
The value function of a coalition $S$ is the marginal (interventional) expectation of the score when the attributes outside $S$ are drawn from a background of $B=50$ training rows, drawn once per dataset and seed and held fixed in every experiment of this paper.
The background is thus part of the definition of the attribution, and the Shapley value $\phi(x)\in\mathbb{R}^d$ of this value function is the exact reference.
A run of a randomised estimator with budget $m$ coalition samples (i.e.\ $m\times B$ model evaluations) returns $\hat\phi(x)$; all of its randomness is in the sampling of coalitions.
Scores are taken in one output space for both $\phi$ and $\hat\phi$: log-odds for logistic regression, the MLP and gradient boosting, and the class-1 probability for the random forest, the quantity that TreeSHAP explains.
Because model class and output space change together, we do not compare families as such.

A reader draws three conclusions from one run: (C1) the top feature; (C2) the top-$k$ set by $|\hat\phi_j|$, with $k=3$ as primary and $k\in\{1,5\}$ as sensitivity ($k=5$ only for $d\ge16$); (C3) the sign of each feature with $|\phi_j|\ge0.1\max_i|\phi_i|$.

\subsection{Single-run correctness and reliability}
For an instance $x$, the \emph{single-run correctness} is $P_c(x)=\Pr_{\text{run}}[\text{top-}k(\hat\phi)=\text{top-}k(\phi)]$, estimated from $R$ independent runs.
The \emph{margin} of $x$ is $g_k(x)=(|\phi|_{(k)}-|\phi|_{(k+1)})/\max_j|\phi_j|$, where $|\phi|_{(i)}$ is the $i$-th largest magnitude.
A small margin makes the top-$k$ set a near-tie, so we also report the \emph{tolerance-aware} correctness $P_c^{\varepsilon}(x)$, which counts a run as correct if it differs from the exact top-$k$ set only by swaps among features whose exact $|\phi_j|$ lies within $\varepsilon\max_i|\phi_i|$ of the $k/(k{+}1)$ boundary ($\varepsilon=0.05$ unless stated).
When this tolerance group contains more than one feature beyond the boundary pair, the attribution is nearly flat and $P_c^{\varepsilon}$ is satisfied vacuously; we report the share of such instances.
\emph{Run-to-run agreement} $A(x)$ is the probability that two independent runs give the same top-$k$ set; it is what a user who reruns sees, and $A\le P_c$ in general.

shown.message:
The main text now fits in 9 pages on `dev` (08237b6), but with no spare room. I haven't offered a version yet, because the figures and tables and some results are still waiting on other roles.

- **Corrections from `experiment-repo`#7:** I applied all of them.
  - The logistic-regression control: `shap` Kernel with `l1_reg=False` and antithetic permutation have zero variance except at the smallest budgets, where the spread is numerical bias. Paired Kernel is not zero-variance.
  - The evaluation-cost unit, the MLP architecture, and the 38-coalition exception for antithetic permutation at German m=32. I also dropped the Clopper–Pearson clause from `design.tex` and the checklist, since no table has those intervals.
  - The m* slope is now stated as grid-dependent for paired Kernel, and the Tobit and probit slopes for the `shap` Kernel explainer are reported as disagreeing. The φ-error slope reading is now "may reflect", and the H1 counts name the estimator.
  - The compute checklist item is filled with about 24 CPU-hours for the main grid and about 34 for the whole study.
- **Floor b versus floor a:** against the `shap` default, a re-drawn background changes the top-3 set more often than a re-run. Against paired Kernel at the same budget it is mixed: 1 lower, 5 higher and 7 unresolved among 13 non-linear cells. I qualified the abstract, introduction, §5.5 and the discussion accordingly.
- **Numbers re-checked:** the headline shares, quartile means, H1 counts, certificate Brier differences and coverage match the current tables.
- **Length:** I cut the abstract and trimmed the results and discussion text.

Still pending:
- `figtab-repo` has a new request (`paper-repo`#7) to rebuild the figures and tables on the current results. `tab3_certificate` and the appendix background figure still show old numbers, so the Appendix B text waits for that.
- `experiment-repo` still owes the ACS Employment MLP floors, floor b by background for the GMSC, German and ACS Employment MLPs, and the final CPU-hours. I'll rewrite the sentence counting the 13 cells, and the compute figures, when they land.

I told `experiment-repo` in #7 what I applied and what I'm waiting on.
